attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The proof still lacks the analytic domination estimate for all reflected gauge-invariant probes actually generated by the Yang-Mills RG construction. In particular, it is not known here that Balaban-style compactness controls nonlocal Wilson-loop products and reflection-plane trace limits with constants uniform enough to make \(\tau_{RG}\) dominate \(\tau_{OS}\).
steps: Fix a finite OS probe \(P=(F_1,\dots,F_m,c)\) in the locked positive-time gauge-invariant algebra, first with supports at distance \(\delta>0\) from the reflection plane.
Use regulated reflection positivity to get \(Q_{a_n,L_n}(I_{a_n,L_n}F,c)\ge0\) for every cutoff in the cofinal sequence.

Decompose the desired convergence as \(|Q_{a_n,L_n}(I_{a_n,L_n}F,c)-Q_S(F,c)|\le A_n(P)+B_n(P)\), where \(A_n\) measures Schwinger functional convergence on the reflected product observable and \(B_n\) measures the error of replacing the cutoff realization/reflection by the locked continuum observable.
Apply OS-probe domination to force \(A_n(P)\to0\) from \(S_{a_n,L_n}\to S\) in \(\tau_{RG}\).
Apply the same-theory condition and asymptotic commutation \(\Theta_{a,L}I_{a,L}\approx I_{a,L}\Theta\) to force \(B_n(P)\to0\).
Attempt to remove the separation restriction by choosing time-mollified approximants \(F_i^{(\delta)}\to F_i\) and passing \(\delta\downarrow0\).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The closed-cone step is valid, but conditional. The missing input is not formal topology; it is a Yang-Mills estimate showing that reflected composite observables lie in the same convergence class as the observables controlled by cutoff removal. The boundary-extension lemma also needs absence or positivity of contact terms at the reflection plane.

assumptions: For each finite list \(F_1,\dots,F_m\in\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lock}}_+\) and coefficients \(c\in\mathbb C^m\), the regulated quadratic form \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)\) is nonnegative.
There is a cofinal cutoff sequence \((a_n,L_n)\) along which \(S_{a_n,L_n}\to S\) in \(\tau_{RG}\).

OS-probe domination: for every finite probe \(P=(F_1, dots,F_m,c)\) there are \(\tau_{RG}\)-seminorms \(p_1, dots,p_N\) and a constant \(C_P\) such that \(|Q_T(P)|\le C_P\max_r p_r(T)\) for all differences of admissible Schwinger functionals \(T\).
The cutoff realization maps commute with reflection in the limit: \(\Theta_{a,L}I_{a,L}F-I_{a,L}\Theta F\to0\) in the probe seminorms relevant to \(P\).
The observable supports are initially taken a positive distance from the reflection plane; extension to boundary-touching probes is deferred to a separate trace/contact-term lemma.
definitions: source object: a net \((S_{a,L})\) of regulated reflection-positive Schwinger functionals for gauge-invariant lattice/block observables, with cutoff realization maps \(I_{a,L}:\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lock}}_+\to\mathcal A_{a,L,+}\).

target object: a continuum Schwinger functional \(S\) satisfying OS positivity on the same gauge-invariant positive-time algebra, hence eligible for the OS Hilbert-space reconstruction with positive Hamiltonian once the remaining OS axioms are verified.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, mediated by convergence of each finite quadratic form \(Q_{S_{a,L}}(I_{a,L}F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\).

same-theory condition: \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lock}}_+\) is fixed before taking limits; \(I_{a,L}\) approximates the identity on continuum gauge-invariant observables and no gauge fixing, quotient completion, or replacement by a smaller positive cone changes the observable theory.

equations.label: finite OS probe
equations.valid_when: The products \((\Theta F_i)F_j\) are in the domain of the continuum Schwinger functional and the reflection map preserves the locked gauge-invariant algebra.

equations.label: RG domination of OS probe
equations.valid_when: The cutoff-removal topology controls the reflected product observables generated by the chosen finite probe.

equations.label: closed-cone consequence
equations.valid_when: The same-theory identification and OS-probe domination both hold for the probe \((F,c)\).

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A decisive falsifier would be a finite reflected gauge-invariant probe \(P\) and a sequence \(S_n\to S\) in \(\tau_{RG}\) such that all \(Q_{S_n}(P)\ge0\) but \(Q_S(P)<0\); this would prove that the proposed topology is not valid for OS passage.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates the non-formal bridge from RG convergence to OS positivity: the closed cone argument is automatic once the RG topology is shown to be at least as strong as the finite-OS-probe topology on the locked algebra.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let \(S_{a,L}\) be finite-volume/cutoff Euclidean Yang-Mills Schwinger functionals on a locked gauge-invariant positive-time observable algebra \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lock}}_+\). Suppose \(S_{a_n,L_n}\to S\) in the RG cutoff-removal topology \(\tau_{RG}\), every \(S_{a_n,L_n}\) is reflection-positive on the corresponding cutoff realization of \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lock}}_+\), and every finite OS quadratic probe is continuous for \(\tau_{RG}\) after the cutoff-to-continuum identification. Then \(S\) is OS-positive on \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lock}}_+\). Equivalently, the RG passage is valid for reflection positivity if \(\tau_{RG}\) dominates the initial topology generated by finite reflected quadratic forms.

assumptions: The locked algebra admits time-mollified approximants \(F^{(\delta)}\to F\) without losing gauge invariance.
The Schwinger distributions obey enough Sobolev/regularity control in the time variables to make the boundary trace operation continuous for reflected products.
Reflection positivity has already been transferred on every away-from-plane algebra \( igcup_{\delta>0}\mathcal A^{\delta}_+\).
definitions: \(\mathcal A^{\delta}_+\): gauge-invariant observables supported in \(t\ge\delta\), for which reflected products avoid coincident reflection-plane singularities.
Trace bound: a uniform estimate allowing \(Q_S(F^{(\delta)}-F,c)\to0\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
No negative contact term: the distributional boundary contribution in \(S((\Theta F)G)\) is either absent or positive semidefinite.

equations.label: boundary approximation of OS forms
equations.valid_when: The trace/contact-term estimate controls the limit as supports approach the reflection plane.

equations.label: extension by closure
equations.valid_when: The approximants remain in the same gauge-invariant algebra and the OS form is continuous in the boundary-approach topology.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is a continuum limit with a reflection-plane contact distribution whose contribution is invisible for separated supports but produces \(Q_S(F,c)<0\) for a boundary-touching observable.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma separates the ultraviolet reflection-plane issue from the main RG-to-OS closed-cone step. It says that the main bridge may first be proved for separated supports, but only if a real trace estimate later closes the gap.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If OS positivity is proved for the subalgebra \(\mathcal A^{\delta}_+\subset\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lock}}_+\) of gauge-invariant observables whose time supports are at distance at least \(\delta>0\) from the reflection plane, and if the continuum Schwinger functional has a reflection-compatible trace bound with no negative contact term at \(t=0\), then OS positivity extends to the full positive-time test algebra by approximating every \(F\in\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lock}}_+\) by \(F^{(\delta)}\in\mathcal A^{\delta}_+\).

assumptions: The loop smearings have bounded geometry: finite length, controlled curvature, and positive distance from the reflection plane.
The RG convergence theorem includes composite gauge-invariant observables, not only elementary curvature insertions.
Multiplication of reflected positive-time observables is continuous in the chosen test algebra.
definitions: Smeared Wilson-loop observable: a gauge-invariant cylindrical functional obtained by averaging holonomies around smooth loops with test density supported in positive time.
Reflected kernel family: the collection of test densities obtained by applying \(\Theta\) to the first factor and multiplying with the second factor in \((\Theta F_i)F_j\).
Uniform kernel control: RG convergence estimates hold with constants depending on finitely many loop geometry and test-function seminorms, not on the cutoff.

equations.label: probe expansion into distribution evaluations
equations.valid_when: The chosen observables admit a finite cylinder/smeared-loop expansion against continuum Schwinger distributions.

equations.label: seminorm control of expansion
equations.valid_when: The RG topology contains the indicated negative-Sobolev or distributional seminorms on compact sets containing the reflected supports.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier would be a nonlocal loop observable whose reflected product cannot be approximated by the distributional observables controlled by RG estimates, even though each unreflected loop observable is controlled separately.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a reduction lemma: it converts the abstract OS-probe domination obligation into the concrete analytic estimates that a Balaban-style multiscale construction would need to supply for gauge-invariant composite observables.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a finite family of smeared Wilson-loop or curvature-polynomial gauge-invariant observables supported away from the reflection plane, the associated OS quadratic form is a finite linear combination of Schwinger distribution evaluations on reflected smearing kernels. Therefore any RG convergence theorem that is uniform on these reflected kernels implies OS-probe domination for that finite family.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this route if an RG compactness theorem can be shown to omit a necessary reflected Wilson-loop or boundary probe, or if a negative reflection-plane contact term is forced by the construction.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the bridge if one proves a uniform estimate bounding every separated finite OS probe by established RG seminorms, plus a trace lemma extending positivity to boundary-touching positive-time observables without changing the gauge-invariant algebra.
control_decision.reason: The branch remains productive because it has identified a specific analytic estimate, \(\tau_{RG}\ge\tau_{OS}\), whose proof or failure decides the interface. Continue, but stop spending effort on the already-formal closed-cone argument.

dependency_updates.description: The dependency splits into a formal closed-cone theorem, now conditionally valid in the finite-OS-probe topology, and a non-formal domination theorem proving \(\tau_{RG}\ge\tau_{OS}\) on reflected gauge-invariant probes.

The algebra must be locked before cutoff removal and must include the reflected products used in OS forms. It is unsafe to prove positivity on a smaller convenient algebra unless a density and same-theory theorem is supplied.

The topology must control finite reflected quadratic probes, including nonlocal loop observables and limits toward the reflection plane. Ordinary convergence on unreflected correlators is not sufficient unless it implies these probe estimates.

falsifiers: falsifier: Find a sequence of reflection-positive regulated Schwinger functionals converging in the advertised RG topology while a finite reflected Wilson-loop quadratic form converges to a negative value; this would show \(\tau_{RG}\) is too weak.

falsifier: Show that the cutoff realization maps \(I_{a,L}\) do not asymptotically commute with time reflection for blocked gauge-invariant observables near \(t=0\), so that positivity is transferred to a different algebra rather than the intended theory.

falsifier: Exhibit a reflection-plane contact term invisible for probes with support distance \(\delta>0\) but negative for a limiting positive-time observable; then away-from-plane positivity is not enough.

falsifier: Prove that RG bounds control only local curvature insertions while the physical gauge-invariant algebra requires nonlocal loop observables whose reflected products are outside the controlled distribution space.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 169 converts the branch's slogan into a precise domination theorem: OS positivity survives cutoff removal exactly when every finite reflected quadratic form is continuous for the actual RG topology after the same-theory observable identification. The formal closed-cone lemma is valid but no longer the bottleneck. The genuine Yang-Mills work is to prove reflected-probe domination for the locked gauge-invariant algebra, first away from the reflection plane and then through a trace/contact-term extension. This gives concrete falsifier tests rather than merely asking whether reflection positivity is preserved.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work on the separated-support Wilson-loop case: write a finite OS probe made of smeared Wilson loops as reflected distribution kernels and test whether known multiscale bounds plausibly control the seminorms \(\|(S_{a,L}-S)_n\|_{-k,K}\) uniformly on those kernels.
